column1: # Ratchet direction: this file must only ever shrink (NEW keys fail the sweep).
# Re-blessed 2026-09-05 after the delInstrText / hyperlink / szCs / inherited-
# invalidity fixes. Full sweep over the 207-pair word_based corpus:
# KEY FORMAT FIX: the previous bless keyed every stem as "<stem>.ours", a name
# scripts/redline-sweep.sh never produces. Every key therefore read as NEW and
# every baseline key as FIXED, so the ratchet reported 74 regressions and 75
# fixes on an unchanged corpus. Normalised, the two sets were identical. Keys
# here are the plain pair_stem the sweep actually emits.
# This baseline records the current state so regressions are detectable. It is
# NOT an assertion that these findings are acceptable. Triage:
#   ~495  r/g/b="0%" colour attributes  — INHERITED: 4 source documents carry
#         them; our output copies them through.
#   ~102  w:Unid undeclared             — OURS: internal PT scratch reaching the
#         serializer bound to the w: prefix, so the pt:* stripper misses it.
#         Traced to document_comparer::compare_documents_impl; the name is built
#         somewhere other than PT::unid(). See KNOWN_ISSUES.md issue 4. OPEN.
#     48  w:ins inside OMML math        — needs triage.
# WHAT RING 2 CANNOT SEE. All five Ring 3 open failures had a CLEAN validator
# report. Word refused them over `w:instrText` under `w:del`, which is
# schema-valid (w:instrText is legal in a run regardless of the run's parent)
# and semantically forbidden (Word wants w:delInstrText and offers to repair
# otherwise). Do not read a clean Ring 2 as "Word will open it".
# Counts by error_id at bless time:
